sentences.text: Hair : The American Tribal Love-Rock Musical is a rock musical with a book and lyrics by James Rado and Gerome Ragni and music by Galt MacDermot .	Galt MacDermot	Galt MacDermot	James Rado	James Rado	Gerome Ragni	Gerome Ragni	rock musical	rock musical

A product of the hippie counterculture and sexual revolution of the late 1960s , several of its songs became anthems of the anti-Vietnam War peace movement .	hippie	hippie	counterculture	Counterculture of the 1960s	sexual revolution	sexual revolution	anti-Vietnam War	Opposition to the Vietnam War	peace movement	peace movement	Vietnam War	Vietnam War

The musical 's profanity , its depiction of the use of illegal drugs , its treatment of sexuality , its irreverence for the American flag , and its nude scene caused much comment and controversy .	sexuality	free love	American flag	American flag

The musical broke new ground in musical theatre by defining the genre of `` rock musical '' , using a racially integrated cast , and inviting the audience onstage for a `` Be-In '' finale .	rock musical	rock musical	musical theatre	musical theatre	Be-In	Human Be-In

Hair tells the story of the `` tribe '' , a group of politically active , long-haired hippies of the `` Age of Aquarius '' living a bohemian life in New York City and fighting against conscription into the Vietnam War .	long-haired	Long hair	Age of Aquarius	Age of Aquarius	bohemian	Bohemianism	conscription	conscription	Vietnam War	Vietnam War

Claude , his good friend Berger , their roommate Sheila and their friends struggle to balance their young lives , loves , and the sexual revolution with their rebellion against the war and their conservative parents and society .	sexual revolution	sexual revolution

Ultimately , Claude must decide whether to resist the draft as his friends have done , or to succumb to the pressures of his parents -LRB- and conservative America -RRB- to serve in Vietnam , compromising his pacifist principles and risking his life .	resist the draft	Conscientious objector	pacifist	Pacifism

After an off-Broadway debut in October 1967 at Joseph Papp 's Public Theater and a subsequent run at the Cheetah nightclub from December 1967 through January 1968 , the show opened on Broadway in April 1968 and ran for 1,750 performances .	off-Broadway	off-Broadway	Joseph Papp	Joseph Papp	Public Theater	The Public Theater	Cheetah	Cheetah (nightclub)	Broadway	Broadway theatre
Simultaneous productions in cities across the United States and Europe followed shortly thereafter , including a successful London production that ran for 1,997 performances .

Since then , numerous productions have been staged around the world , spawning dozens of recordings of the musical , including the 3 million-selling original Broadway cast recording .	Broadway	Broadway theatre	original Broadway cast recording	Hair The Original Broadway Recording
